instruction: I need help decreasing the font size of all text in my document by 2 points to fit more content on each page. Can you assist with this formatting change?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Decreases all text font size by 2 points. Verified using heuristic: average font size should be in 9-12pt range (reduced from typical 11-14pt). Full verification would require comparing with original font sizes.

llm_judge_reasons: Cannot verify the specific requirement of '2 point decrease' - metric only checks if average font size falls in 9-12pt range, which is a weak heuristic
Missing baseline comparison - evaluator has no access to original font sizes to verify actual decrease amount
Expected value 'decrease_amount: 2' is never used in the metric logic - metric ignores this parameter entirely
Will produce false positives - passes if document originally had 10pt fonts (no change) or was reduced by any amount landing in 9-12pt
Will produce false negatives - fails if original document had 8pt fonts correctly reduced to 6pt
Logical flaw: instruction explicitly requires 'decrease by 2 points' but evaluator can only guess if 'some reduction occurred' based on final size ranges
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add a 'preconfig' step to capture original font sizes before task execution, then compare before/after in the metric
Store original document font sizes in expected.rules (e.g., analyze the source file during task generation)
Modify metric to compare result font sizes against baseline and verify each is exactly 2pt smaller
Alternative: Change instruction to 'ensure all text is between 9-12pt' to match what the evaluator actually checks
